mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is negative, or if the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within two months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of HOUST and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1%, signals a potential inflationary pressure without sufficient monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL increases and low FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strong consumer demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised upwards.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS shows sustained growth, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
